title: The logarithmic cost of componentwise constraints in finite de Finetti approximation

comparators.scope: Twelve fixed explicit targets covering the eight nonexempt numbered results and all three required supplemental connections. Excludes the full Corollary 3.6.
The arbitrary-Borel nonidentical-product logarithmic lower bound with an added premise. Rejection detail: extra premise on Paper06.Challenge.noniid_logarithmic.
The same nonidentical-product contract with an intentionally unauthorized proof dependency. Rejection detail: unauthorized_noniid axiom.

main_results.scope: Normalized posterior preserves the linear constraints at every positive-mass observation, for any unobserved site and observed subset on finite coordinates.
A Borel probability measure on the affine slice satisfies the extended-KL entropy bound, including singular laws and null observations.
One admissible matching law, chosen before k and the mixing measure, satisfies both logarithmic lower bounds for 2 ≤ k, k² ≤ n, and the stated prime/parameter conditions.
Normalized edge law and uniform endpoint-permutation mixture satisfy exchangeability and lifted fixed-input componentwise constraints.
Unique-slope incidence count over every finite field, stochastic-channel decomposition, and the product-event/classical-maximum/beta bounds.
Matching factorial moments and arbitrary Borel-mixture union bound imply the stated KL lower bound under the beta hypothesis, including p = 1 and singular q = 0.
No uniform bound of the stated sublogarithmic form exists, using admissible matching laws along divergent primes.

One Borel measure works for every allowed k, with finite nonempty input-dependent output fibers, zero input masses, componentwise constraints, exchangeability, and exact sampling cost including k = M.
Logarithmic lower bounds for arbitrary Borel mixtures of nonidentical feasible product factors; exact two-point matching law and convergence of the optimal error to zero.
Elementary exponent and constant algebra only; the full corollary requires the external stronger finite-field CHSH incidence theorem and is not asserted.
